name: ZZRC Wrecked Legs - Post Weekend Recovery Ride
description:
Welcome to our  ZZRC Wrecked Legs 2.5-2.7wkg. This is a group ride, not a race, where we encourage riding together. 

Our rides are open to all riders, the category enforcement merely allows us to ensure a safe and quality ride for you the riders and for our group.

In 2015 ZZRC was founded and are one of the oldest established clubs on Zwift .

YELLOW BEACON will pace between 2.5-2.7 on the ride , with a possible increase of watts on inclines or sprints  , but the average for the whole ride is as advertised

We strongly promote group riding so on most of our rides we will use the Fence to help encourage that. Using a fence ensures that the ride is not over paced . 

In the event of falling off the back of the main group , you will need to pace well over group pace to bridge the gap and catch . 

This js a Cat C medium paced group ride . It is not a slow paced Cat D Ride . 

Our rides do not allow the use of TT Bikes as they do not draft and will require you to push harder on the ride, and in these instances our Sweeps will not be able to help you . 

Mountain bikes operate very similarly, minimum draft so more watts (effort) will be required for the ride and any chase backs to group . 

All our rides have a 30 minute late join feature which allows you to rejoin if you have technical issues or you find yourself out of the group in the early stages of the ride. Using this feature SHOULD teleport you back into the main group with our YELLOW BEACON . 

Sweepers are not in operation on this ride so please consider using late join in the first 30 mins or make a small group of your own. 

We love to have a chat on our rides so join us on our dedicated discord 
  https://discord.gg/QdeS3PtXTX

TOP TIPS

1) Stay close to the ride leader (or just in front on climbs), don’t let a gap form and the elastic snap!

2) Stay away from the Fence – We don’t like to fry anyone 

3) Most important of all . . . HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.

#zzrc

Don’t forget to join our ZZRC-We Pace Not Race Facebook page and our club on the companion app

name: Mountain Massif structured training:  Threshold Pyramidal
description:
Created by Matteo Cigala, from Cigala Cycling, this structured training session is designed to help you cycle at a higher intensity.  For coaching and all your training needs visit https://coaching.cigalacycling.com/trainsmarterridefaster

About the session:
This session develops aerobic readiness, controlled tempo and threshold exposure, and progressive tempo endurance. The warm up prepares the athlete for early intensity changes. The single tempo and threshold efforts elevate heart rate and activate muscular engagement without creating unnecessary fatigue. The main set uses structured rising-duration tempo blocks to build aerobic strength, sustained power control, and the ability to manage intensity changes smoothly. Recovery intervals ensure quality and repeatability across both rounds. The cool down supports gradual heart-rate reduction and full metabolic clearance.
Session details:
Warm Up 
5 minutes 40–65% CP 100–110 rpm

Single Efforts 
Tempo: 2 minutes at 80% CP, free cadence 
Threshold: 1 minute at 95% CP, free cadence

Recovery 
5 minutes 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

Main Set (Repeat 2 Times) 
1 minute at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
1 minute at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
2 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
2 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
3 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm
3 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
2 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
2 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
1 minute at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
1 minute at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm

Recovery Between 
Sets 5 minutes 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

Cool Down 
3 minutes 40–55% CP 100–110 rpm

Total Time: 62 minutes 

Key coaching cues: 
Keep transitions between intensities smooth and controlled. Hold steady power during tempo and threshold efforts without drifting upward. Maintain relaxed upper-body posture and consistent breathing throughout. During the main set, focus on smooth cadence and stable power as durations increase. Use recoveries to reset technique and breathing before the next block.

Safety Note: 
Only undertake vigorous exercise if you are fit and healthy to do so. If you are at all unsure, consult a Physician or Doctor first. All training equipment including Bikes and Turbo trainers should be in full working order. Do not use any piece of equipment that does not come up to the required standard.
More information:
For more information check out the Mountain Massif website www.mountainmassif.com, follow on Instagram @mountain_massif, Facebook @mountainmassif and join our Zwift Club, by clicking the following link https://www.zwift.com/clubs/mountainmassif/home
To record all your training data and chart your progress, consider using the TrainingPeaks app or Vekta by following the link https://joinvekta.com/

name: Rowe & King - Monday Mixer
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

Rowe & King's Monday Mixer is a short but focused session, full of structure. In terms of physical stress - the session is regarded as "moderate" - one that can be completed following a hard Sunday ride, and should not leave your legs too fatigued come Tuesday. This session is regarded as 'High Intensity Interval Training' (HIIT) and fits in perfectly alongside longer endurance rides on the weekend.

In terms of physical stress - the session is regarded as "moderate" - one that can be completed following a hard Sunday ride, and should not leave your legs too fatigued come Tuesday. 

This session is regarded as 'High Intensity Interval Trainng' (HIIT) and fits in perfectly alongside longer endurance rides on the weekend. 

WORKOUT DESIGNER

This session is designed by Rowe & King Head Coach, Courtney Rowe who has been coaching cyclists for over 30 years from beginner to professionals, and is a firm believer in quality over quantity. 

Courtney is 29 x Welsh Champion, 5 x British Champion, 4 x European Champion and has 5 World Championship medals in his trophy cabinet! 

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins.  Everyone stays together regardless of power output.   That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other.  Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.

HELPFUL HINT

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level.   

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: SZR Evening Joyride
description:
Welcome to the SZR (Swedish Zwift Riders) and the Evening Joyride which is the oldest SZR Event, and it started in September 2015 for the first time.
This ride is a ride for all categories of riders, that is why we have a lot of categories to choose from in this ride so make sure to pick a category that fits your needs.

- The goal with the SZR group ride is to focus on the group and keeping the group together the entire ride.
- Make sure to choose the correct group. We split up in four groups B, C, D and E group.
Group B -> 3.2 - 4.0 w/kg
Group C -> 2.5 - 3.0 w/kg
Group D -> 2.1 - 2,4 w/kg
Group E -> 1.5 - 2.0 w/kg

- This is a social group ride and not a race. Staying close to the ride leader is the key.
- Please follow the ride leaders instructions at all times.
- After steep hills we focus on keeping the group together and soft pedal to let the group come together again.
Use our discord if you like to have a chat with the people on the ride
https://discord.gg/DQHybQT

name: Master Your Power
description: Ride smarter. Find your rhythm. Unlock your indoor potential. Whether you’re recovering from a hard race, looking for an activation session or ready for a more demanding workout, you can adjust the intensity to suit your fitness and training goals.No racing experience required. Just bring your curiosity, your bike and a willingness to learn. Train smart. Ride strong. We Love Cycling.

name: Ventouro Social Group Ride
description:
A fun morning ride to get the legs turning for the week. Enjoy being part of a group and riding to your ability. The ride is generally led by ex Pro Tour rider and double Olympian Tim Gudsell, or one of Ventouro’s great crew.

The ride starts steady and moderate pace most around the flat streets of London (2-2.5w/kg) no need to load up the watts more than 100w. There will be a fence on just after the start so please respect it. It comes off after 14km.
It starts climbing at KM 13. With 5km up hill and the last 2km being the steepest. Then a fast run down to the finish.
It will split on the hill, so you can go for gold to the finish, or keep it in zone and make your way up at a steady pace. Enjoy!

Ventouro is an adventure cycling business offering guided tours of the world's most beautiful destinations. From weekend retreats in New Zealand's wine regions, to week-long journeys through the fjords of Norway, The Great Wall of China, or the French Alps.

From a standing start in 2014 Ventouro has established itself as a globally recognised luxury-cycling business with an established high-net-worth client-base in America, China, Australia and New Zealand.

name: DBR Monday Race
description:
Welcome to DBR Monday Race.
All will start with 1 minute between RS categories. Expect each race to be highly competitive and have fun.

Categories
Each race will be using Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) for categorization.
race up a category, if your RS is at the top end of a category. Or if you simply desire an added challenge.
- A:1000 =< 690
- B:690<520
- C:520<350
- D:350<180
- E:180<=0

Your Zwift Racing Score is determined by how much success you have in races.
better against people with higher ZRS, then your ZRS may increase. If you place worse than people with lower ZRS, then your score might decrease. Read more about ZRS here - https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh <https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-score-faq-BkG9_Rqrh>
If your ZRS increases past a category boundary during the series, your points earned will not transfer to the new category with you.

RULES:
Smart trainer or power meter is required. zPower will be removed.
Heart rate monitors are compulsory for all categories.
No TT bikes unless it's a TT event.
You need to have a registered account with Zwiftpower.com and accept their terms and conditions to be in the results of the race.

Misc.
Race organizers may request riders in all categories to provide a dual recording or a matching RL effort (Strava) in order to verify a Zwift race effort. Failure to comply may result in disqualification from the event. Failure to provide a dual recording or RL effort on three requests may result in disqualification from future events, until a dual recording with a matching effort is provided.
Race organizers may exclude a rider from the results, due to poor sportsmanship. Examples may be bad language, sandbagging or other behavior of a disruptive manner.

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Alpe | Week 5
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from
Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and
climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.
Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift
These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to
play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder
bike choices.
• No draft regardless of bike.
• No power up’s just you and your watts.
• Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only
10km, elevation is primary focus.
• Category enforced, must wear HRM.
• Zwift Power league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to Zwift ITT
Racing. Links below, each month the leagues will be reset. An excel backup is available
on Torturefest Cult discord ITT Climbing room.
• Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice
dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
• What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has
multiple climbs?
• How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?
One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing
Russian roulette style.

name: ZZRC Spin Out Sub 2
description:
Welcome to our ZZRC Spin Out Sub 2. This is a group ride, not a race, where we encourage riding together.

Our rides are open to all riders, the category enforcement merely allows us to ensure a safe and quality ride for you the riders and for our group.

In 2015 ZZRC was founded and are one of the oldest established clubs on Zwift .

YELLOW BEACON will pace between 1.7-1.9 on the ride , with a possible increase of watts on inclines or sprints , but the average for the whole ride will be sub 2 .

We strongly promote group riding so on most of our rides we will use the Fence to help encourage that. Using a fence ensures that the ride is not over paced .

In the event of falling off the back of the main group , you will need to pace well over group pace to bridge the gap and catch .

This is where our awesome ZZRC sweeps and Ride Buddies will help you return to group using their draft. They will give you clear encouraging instructions to aid this process .

Our crew are a caring bunch who dedicated a lot of hours to this club , but want you to have the best ride experience on Zwift

You will be fully supported and encouraged throughout the ride by the Leader, Sweeps and Ride Buddies .

Our rides do not allow the use of TT Bikes as they do not draft and will require you to push harder on the ride, and in these instances our Sweeps will not be able to help you .

Mountain bikes operate very similarly, minimum draft so more watts (effort) will be required for the ride and any chase backs to group .

All our rides have a 30 minute late join feature which allows you to rejoin if you have technical issues or you find yourself out of the group in the early stages of the ride. Using this feature SHOULD teleport you back into the main group with our YELLOW BEACON .


We love to have a chat on our rides so join us on our dedicated discord channel for our sub 2
https://discord.gg/RJ3dhbjCEp


TOP TIPS

1) Stay close to the ride leader (or just in front on climbs), don’t let a gap form and the elastic snap!

2) Stay away from the Fence – We don’t like to fry anyone

3) Most important of all . . . HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.

#zzrc

Don’t forget to join our ZZRC-We Pace Not Race Facebook page and our club on the companion app

description:

If you want the experience of a group ride with no drop and no nasty fence then this might be just what you are looking for. Our ZHCC Rubber Band Club has the “rubber-band” activated which means that no matter what level you are, you will be able to keep up and the group WILL STAY TOGETHER. The rubber band allows you to ride at your own pace, slow or fast and you are guaranteed to stay in the group.

In this supportive environment it’s a great way of completing a full 1-hour ride knowing you won’t get dropped or get dragged along by those naughty fliers!
ZHCC do not race each other, we ride as one, have fun and enjoy a group ride.
The ZHCC gang look forward to riding with you.

name: ZZRC Endurance Express
description:
ZZRC Endurance Express | 3.0-3.2 W/kg

Welcome aboard the ZZRC Endurance Express , this is our winter endurance series designed to help you tick away those winter base miles with company… so expect a brisk, constant pace not a race 

“Endurance” here refers to the time spent riding or the distance covered. Expect a longer ride at a steady, purposeful pace. The advertised 3.0-3.2 W/kg is the leader’s pace; whether that feels like an endurance effort for you will depend on your fitness and FTP.

ZZRC was founded in 2015 and is one of Zwift’s longest-established clubs. We welcome riders who are comfortable with the advertised pace and ready to enjoy the journey together.

Pace and group riding

The Yellow Beacon will pace the ride at an average of 3.0-3.2 W/kg. Effort may rise briefly on climbs, but the overall average will remain within the advertised range.

We use the Fence to help keep the group together and prevent the pace from creeping up.

There are no sweeps on this ride. If you fall behind, catching back on will require an effort above the group’s pace. If you cannot rejoin, settle into a comfortable rhythm with riders around you. We will still be in touch through the on-screen messages.

Bike choice and late join

TT bikes are not permitted because they do not draft. Choose a road bike to make the most of riding with the group.

A 30-minute late join window is available if you have a technical issue or lose the group early in the ride. Rejoining during that window should place you back with the main group and the Yellow Beacon.

Top tips

1. Stay close to the Yellow Beacon and anticipate climbs to avoid gaps opening.
2. Give the Fence some space—we don’t want anyone getting fried!
3. Have drinks and fuel ready for the advertised duration or distance.
4. Settle into your rhythm, enjoy the company and watch the kilometres add up.

We love a chat, so join us on Discord. You can also find ZZRC – We Pace Not Race on Facebook and join our club in the Zwift Companion app.

All aboard the Endurance Express—we pace, not race!

Stay for a little while or a long while - either way, we look forward to having you in our draft!
Our Spotify playlist is filled with different tracks each week and can be found here https://open.spotify.com/playlist/1HVldYQmN6BBHW0FPeg3fP?si=C_IS5QxvSuKtb07oOix-Vw&utm_source=copy-link. Our top tip is to follow the playlist so you can find it easily each week.
Keep within the bunch for the best draft effect, and enjoy practising your control and pacing as you keep yourself within reach of the Beacon. We will average about 36-38km/h within the bunch, sitting comfortably under 2.5w/kg. Our sweeps will do their best to help you back, just give them a yell to let them know - have your Companion App open to join in the onscreen chat, drop Ride-Ons and watch the map for your location in relation to the beacon bunch.
Remember, it's not a race, there are no winners, just a group of people who enjoy each other's company!

Follow TBR at thebigring.cc to learn more about our events, read ride reports and leave feedback.

name: The Euro Chop by AHDR
description:
The Euro Chop by AHDR
The famous Chop Race by AHDR is now in Europe! 
Being ""in the chop"" is an Aussie expression that you won't read about in the UCI rulebook. It's one of the many nuances of bike racing that only comes with experience.

Sometimes when you're in a race and find yourself in the final break-away bunch you might get asked ""are we in the chop?"" or ""are we chopping it?"". This is referring to collusion between the lead riders to work together until the finish. Many times a break-away will be doomed in the final kilometres because everyone starts playing cat and mouse, attacking, sitting up, etc.

But all that goes out the window in the last lap. This is generally where the group comes together and the final push begins. Working together goes out the window and is every man or woman for themselves for the final sprint to the line.

The Euro Chop by AHDR feature mostly flat fast time-based handicap race. Do you always get blown out the back on the start of a multi grade race trying to hang onto the guy going with A grade pushing 5w/kg. Well not on The Chop. Released in Grades there are time splits from D to A with the intention of all coming together at the end for the big finish. Each Grade wears a different AHDR/Zwift kit making each grade easily identifiable on who's wheel you want to catch if they go past.

Races happen on Monday evenings. No single race has been the same. Many variables are at play on The Chop including course (which is generally a flat course), race numbers, and the inevitable sandbaggers. It has been called a team time trail and cat and mouse but the real racers know it only as ""THE CHOP"". Do you have what it takes to take the glory?

#ahdr

Your Zwift Racing Score is determined by how much success you have in races.
better against people with higher ZRS, then your ZRS may increase. If you place worse than people with lower ZRS, then your score might decrease.
Read more about ZRS here: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/racing-BkG9_Rqrh
If your ZRS increases past a category boundary during the series, your points earned will not transfer to the new category with you.

RULES:

name: Velos Tour de Friends
description:
Newer to Zwift and working to improve your fitness? Recovering from injury? Or just want to ease into the week with a friendly & supportive group? Then come join our gentle D-paced tour around Zwift’s worlds, sharing laughs and fun adventures. We may depart as strangers, but will finish as friends. Each week we feature a pub quiz, play along and have some fun while learning a bit of trivia!

This ride is designed as a step up for beginners with some experience who are looking for something a bit faster. Continuing to challenge yourself is key to getting stronger. Trust that you are joining a ride where the leaders stick to the advertised pace, and where strong sweeps are always available to help anyone struggling at the back finish. We support everyone on our rides so you leave feeling happier than when you started.

We will average 14-18 mph (1.5 w/kg), depending on the course. Late join is available up to 30 minutes in. We hope to welcome you to the Velos family!

Join us at teamvelos.co.uk

Staying in the draft is essential for this event

name: TBR Happy Snappy Hour
description:
Welcome to TBR Happy Snappy Hour!
The leader (yellow beacon) will hold a pace of 2w/kg during the entire ride. Join the leader for an easy ride!
If you want to challenge yourself then try to chase the red beacon during the efforts each lap. Each effort ends at a sprint or KOM banner (different length each lap). The leader will announce the start of each effort.
Join this ride for the fun and jokes or to train for a race - it's up to you!

eventSubgroups.description:
TBR presents friendly Race Training. Races are often decided on snappy 1-5min efforts, so lets train this! We ride at an all-cat friendly base-pace of 1.5-2wkg, then mix in sharp efforts towards Banners. First aim is always to break new personal Power Records. No matter which category you belong to, we support you to make you stronger!
Visit thebigring.cc for ride reports and more fun events.

name: ZZRC Easy Rollers 1.5
description:
Welcome to our ZZRC Easy Rollers 1.5. This is a group ride, not a race, where we encourage riding together.

Our rides are open to all riders, the category enforcement merely allows us to ensure a safe and quality ride for you the riders and for our group.

In 2015 ZZRC was founded and are one of the oldest established clubs on Zwift.

YELLOW BEACON will pace between 1.3-1.5. on the ride, with a possible increase of watts on inclines or sprints, but the average for the whole ride will be 1.5

We strongly promote group riding so on most of our rides we will use the Fence to help encourage that. Using a fence ensures that the ride is not over paced.

In the event of falling off the back of the main group, you will need to pace well over group pace to bridge the gap and catch.

This is where our awesome ZZRC sweeps and Ride Buddies will help you return to group using their draft. They will give you clear encouraging instructions to aid this process.

Our crew are a caring bunch who dedicated a lot of hours to this club, but want you to have the best ride experience on Zwift

You will be fully supported and encouraged throughout the ride by the Leader, Sweeps and Ride Buddies.

Our rides do not allow the use of TT Bikes as they do not draft and will require you to push harder on the ride, and in these instances our Sweeps will not be able to help you.

Mountain bikes operate very similarly, minimum draft so more watts (effort) will be required for the ride and any chase backs to group.

All our rides have a 30 minute late join feature which allows you to rejoin if you have technical issues or you find yourself out of the group in the early stages of the ride. Using this feature SHOULD teleport you back into the main group with our YELLOW BEACON.

We love to have a chat on our rides so join us on our dedicated discord channel
https://discord.gg/teHeHABDHc

TOP TIPS

Stay close to the ride leader (or just in front on climbs), don’t let a gap form and the elastic snap!
Stay away from the Fence – We don’t like to fry anyone
Most important of all… HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.
#zzrc

Don’t forget to join our ZZRC-We Pace Not Race Facebook page and our club on the companion app

name: Zwift TT Club Racing - Urumaze
description:
The Time Trial. Cycling’s true leveler - just you and your legs versus everyone else in the field.

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

name: EVO CC Sprint Race Series
description:
CATEGORY ENFORCEMENT IS ENABLED FOR ALL EVO RACES!

What is Category Enforcement? 

Category Enforcement will prevent Zwifters from entering a category they are not eligible for.  Our goal is to increase fairness in racing.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

- Zwift checks a racer's past performance using VO2 max and FTP to determine their race category.
- Racers can join a category at or above their category. For example, if you are "C" category, you can race in C, B, or A category. You will not be able to race in the D category and the option to join will be absent.

Welcome to EVO sprintrace series. Shorter more compact races for the rider looking for an effective high intensity race. Start fast, hang on in the middle, then sprint for the win at the finish. Expect to push your heart rate to its maximum. Sprinkle a few of these into your training plan and watch your fitness grow.

To make racing as fair as possible we have enforced a few minor rules that will result in automatic disqualification on ZwiftPower.

All riders must wear a heart rate monitor
Riding in an incorrect category.

zPower riders will be disqualified in A, B, and C Podium. zPower is allowed in the D category. Race details and final results will be available at www.zwiftpower.com

#evo

name: Cheesecake Extra Slice
description:
Cheesecake Extra Slice is a fun group ride at an average power of around 3w/kg, but with some optional sprints along the way! Definitely a great way to build your sprint power, or if you just want to ride in the draft with the yellow beacon then that is totally fine also.

There is usually plenty of chat in the bunch for those who enjoy the social side of riding. But if you’ve got a confetti allergy then be warned – there will be some serious confetti being tossed around after each sprint with PBs coming in thick and fast! And if you’ve got anything left in your legs at the end, there might even be an opportunity for a gradual lifting of the pace in the final minutes.

Late join available for up to 30 mins after the ride start. All welcome!

name: Zwift Crit Racing Club - Castle Crit
description:
It's Crit time! Come and join in the fun on a number of multi-lap short routes. Get ready to dig deep and push to the finish line!

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

name: RollCo: Rolling Segments
description:
One route. One segment. One week to set your best time.

Every week we'll reveal a new featured segment exclusively through the Rolling Collective Zwift Club. Joining the club is the best way to stay up to date, receive event notifications, and never miss the next challenge. During the group ride you'll tackle the featured segment as it appears on the route, then compare your fastest effort against the rest of the community.
https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ba188519-9c89-4898-a1a7-9e84fc412bc6/home

These events are designed to be relaxed and community-driven. There may not always be an official ride leader, so think of them as an open group ride where everyone heads out to take on the week's challenge at their own pace.

Once you've crossed the segment, head over to the Rolling Collective Discord to log your fastest time on the community leaderboard. Watch the standings evolve throughout the week, compare your effort with other riders, and see if you can climb a few more places.
Discord: https://discord.gg/qdGrM7NaAG

Ride it. Log it. Climb the leaderboard.

name: Monday Run Club
description:
Start your week off right with a group run hosted by the Zwift Runners Facebook Group. We’ll ease into another week of training alongside the community while actively recovering from any long runs you might have had during the weekend. With runs in seven time slots with four pace groups each (A being the fastest and D being the slowest), there’s an event for everyone. 

Pace Groups
A) 7.5–8.5 mph // 12–14 kph
B) 7–7.5 mph // 10.5–12 kph
C) 6–6.5 mph // 9.5–10.5 kph
D) 5–5.5 mph // 8–9 kph

We’ll be using workout mode throughout these runs so everyone can easily determine their speed. Though these runs utilize a mostly steady pace, there will be some speed changes for variety.

If you have any questions about this event or want to find out more about Zwift Run in general, then please visit the Zwift Runners Facebook Group or zwift.com/run

name: PACK Run: 5k Monday
description:
New to running, coming back after some time off, or simply want a nice warm up or cool down session? Join us as we spend 30 minutes moving the legs in this slow-paced, social event. The goal of the event is to encourage folks to move. 

The leader will average 8kph (7:30min/km) // 5mph (12min/mile) and we encourage runners to go at their own pace if the average pace is too fast and/or use a run/walk strategy.

FULL DESCRIPTION

New to running, coming back after some time off, or simply want a nice warm up or cool down session? Join us as we spend 30 minutes moving the legs in this slow-paced, social event. The goal of the event is to encourage folks to move. 

The leader will average 8kph (7:30min/km) // 5mph (12min/mile) for the duration and it is expected everyone will stay together. This is a timed event, so we encourage runners to go at their own pace if the average pace is too fast and/or use a run/walk strategy.

**Note: if you utilize a run/walk strategy, please start with the walking portion so that you are not overrunning the group on each interval.**

Put your black and orange tops and socks on and let's get moving!

name: TEAM VTO POWERPUSH
description:
⚡️🚴🏼‍♂️💨 POWER PUSH! 🚴🏼‍♂️💨⚡️
Looking for a Group Ride that is different to the rest? You've found it! 👍🏻

We’re building a team...... a TIGHT-KNIT team 💨. We aim to break records over the 7.1km timed Fuego Flats Reverse segment. (The aim of the this ride is to take as many riders as possible with us under 9 mins). We start with a lap and a half to settle the group, recon the course and talk tactics. The hammer drops at about 40 mins and the TEAM TIME TRIAL starts.
As a group we aim to PUSH over 50KPH (31MPH) and hold it all the way to the finish arch. This requires TEAMWORK, POWER and DETERMINATION. You will need to dig deep!

Team VTO value FUN, FRIENDSHIP and DETERMINATION. We welcome athletes from around the world 🙏🏻 🌎

Join our Zwift Club - Team VTO (on your companion app 👉🏻📲 https://www.zwift.com/clubs/151ca95c-f6de-4fe2-ae88-a769e367f439/home

To be involved in our community (+ claim your prizes), join our FB group
www.facebook.com/groups/thenewzwifttrioz/

Absolutely Everyone is welcome! 🙏🏻

name: NPRC - Run Every Day Powered By NoblePro
description:
Come and join the fastest growing running club on Zwift.  With a choice of 5 or 10k you can pick your distance. Whether you are a beginner or experienced runner come and join us, you can run at whatever pace you like, it’s not a race unless you want it to be!

Each day is a different route and as new routes are released the courses will change to allow you to bag that badge.

You will run in our in game NPRC jersey and if you complete the event you get to keep it to wear wherever you like.

We also hold special events where you can win an actual jersey to wear in real life.

NPRC Facebook – We have a facebook group where you can join and talk about all things running.  Share your stories and get help and advice.

https://www.facebook.com/groups/1223724692417314/

NoblePro: - We are a team focused on elevating running through our treadmills and digital platforms. We create treadmills loved by runners and the wider running community for quality engineered hardware features and advanced software integration to give you the freedom to train with the apps you love.
https://www.noble-pro.com/

Kinni:- In a fitness world where treadmill bluetooth integration can be a confusing place, we aim to provide you with the ability to effortlessly connect. You can run structured treadmill workouts, connect and integrate with your favourite bluetooth fitness apps such as Zwift, Rouvy, Kinomaps and many more. We are focused on progress and advancement in integration, connectivity and control.
https://kinni.co/https://kinni.co/devices/ - To see if your treadmill is compatible to link to Zwift.

Join the NoblePro Running Club (NPRC) - https://www.zwift.com/clubs/e7829ccd-bce4-4244-9ccf-4cdc3ef148ff/home

description:

name: The Grind Finale
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

This session aims to replicate the demands of a mountain bike ride / event. 

Mountain biking generally involves far more variations in effort compared with road riding - so plenty of surges and time spent being over geared! We also spend a lot of time on and off the power, so short spells going  hard to get over an obstacle, followed by a freewheel or very low power on a descent or little dip.

We touch upon all of these aspects in todays session, as we start off alternating every 30 seconds between riding hard at a low cadence, and riding easy - as if we are riding through an undulating single track. Then we make a ramp in effort, which finishes with a 30 second near max effort up a steep, rocky banking!

WORKOUT DESIGNER

Matt Rowe - Heavily involved in cycling for the past 25 years, Matt represented Great Britain at the Junior World Championships before graduating to the pro ranks. Matt draws on his extensive race experience to help amateur cyclists around the world achieve their personal goals. 

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop. 

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level. For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: RO4H Restoration Ride
description:
The RO4H Restoration Ride is a chance to do your body a favor following all the hard riding you did over the weekend. Participating in this low-intensity ride will provide some active recovery to your body and allow your mind to relax in a friendly, casual, supportive, and respectful atmosphere.

This restorative ride is ultimately a social ride, and everyone is welcome to participate. The pace will vary depending on terrain and route but will have an average speed of about 15-18 mph/24-29 kph. We’ll remain sub 2 W/kg on any climbs and climbs will have sub 4% average grade. Despite this being a recovery pace for some, it will be a challenging effort for others. You should be prepared to meet the listed average speed. Being a social ride, we strive to ride together to take advantage of the strong group draft within the peloton. We’ll aim to be a no-drop ride. This ride is certainly not a race, and we discourage fliers.
We are proud of our strong sweeper team. Part of the RO4H ride philosophy is that we do not want anyone to ride alone -- unless they choose so. Our sweepers will either help riders bridge to the peloton or form a second pace group, so you do not ride alone.

So go ahead and join the RO4H Restoration Ride -- where friends are plentiful, and we are Better Together.

Check out the RO4H ride schedule: https://www.zwift.com/events/tag/ro4h.

FB: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ZwiftRideOn4Health/.

name: The HERD Mellow Monday
description:
Are you a Herdling with substance? All endurance, not so much about speed? Whether you are trying to get into shape, become a smaller version of yourself or just looking to ride with some like-minded people, this is the ride for you. 
 
The goal to have fun, be comfortable with who we are, and blow off some Monday steam.
Pace is 1.0 – 1.3. Non Clyde/Athena riders are welcome, but recognize this is a place for us to feel welcome and comfortable. We will ride a mix of courses, because just because we are larger, doesn’t mean we can’t climb!

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Alpe | Week 5
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from
Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and
climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.
Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift
These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to
play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder
bike choices.
• No draft regardless of bike.
• No power up’s just you and your watts.
• Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only
10km, elevation is primary focus.
• Category enforced, must wear HRM.
• Zwift Power league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to Zwift ITT
Racing. Links below, each month the leagues will be reset. An excel backup is available
on Torturefest Cult discord ITT Climbing room.
• Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice
dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
• What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has
multiple climbs?
• How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?
One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing
Russian roulette style.

name: USMeS Back to Base
description:
Welcome to USMeS Back to Base!!

Monday means it’s time to report for duty...but what’s on the training schedule depends on where we are in the month.
Most Mondays, we’re heading Back to Base for a steady D paced group ride. On the last Monday of every month, however, Basic Training gets vertical, and we head to the Alpe.

BACK TO BASE - Most Mondays of the Month (except the last)
✅ Pace: D
✅ Average: 1.8–2.2 w/kg
✅ Duration: 60 minutes

Back to Base is all about getting the group together and starting the week as a unit. We aim to finish with an overall average of 1.8–2.2 w/kg, but that doesn’t mean we’re afraid to have a little fun along the way. We’ll push a little on the climbs; segments are fair game, and if there’s a sprint banner ahead… well, sometimes orders become optional. 😏

Make your move, have your fun, then fall back in quickly. The goal is to keep the group together, respect the leader and work as one unit.

ALPE BASIC TRAINING - Last Monday of Every Month
Once a month, Back to Base gets replaced by Alpe Basic Training... and Basic Training means we’re going UP.

🎖️ Mission: 1 Lap of the Alpe
🎖️ Target Average: 2.0–2.2 w/kg
🎖️ No Fence

Riders of all abilities are welcome. Our two yellow beacons will hold approximately the advertised 2.0–2.2 w/kg average, but there is no fence and no requirement to stay with them.

Want to stay with the drill instructors? Fall in. Want to attack the Alpe and see what you’ve got? Permission granted. Want to settle into your own rhythm and just get yourself to the top? That counts too.

There’s only one real assignment at Alpe Basic Training....Get to the summit.
Different Monday. Different mission. Same USMeS crew.

BE LIMITLESS

#conqueringlimits #challengeaccepted #embracethesuck

Join us for our weekly Monday after-work recovery ride, designed to help you reset after a weekend of racing or hard efforts. With options ranging from 30 to 60 minutes, these rides are structured to keep things steady, controlled, and accessible.

Spin the legs out, keep it conversational, and connect with others across the USA Cycling community. Riders of all levels are welcome, and there’s always a group to roll with.

name: Mountain Massif structured training:  Threshold Pyramidal
description:
Created by Matteo Cigala, from Cigala Cycling, this structured training session is designed to help you cycle at a higher intensity.  For coaching and all your training needs visit https://coaching.cigalacycling.com/trainsmarterridefaster

About the session:
This session develops aerobic readiness, controlled tempo and threshold exposure, and progressive tempo endurance. The warm up prepares the athlete for early intensity changes. The single tempo and threshold efforts elevate heart rate and activate muscular engagement without creating unnecessary fatigue. The main set uses structured rising-duration tempo blocks to build aerobic strength, sustained power control, and the ability to manage intensity changes smoothly. Recovery intervals ensure quality and repeatability across both rounds. The cool down supports gradual heart-rate reduction and full metabolic clearance.
Session details:
Warm Up 
5 minutes 40–65% CP 100–110 rpm

Single Efforts 
Tempo: 2 minutes at 80% CP, free cadence 
Threshold: 1 minute at 95% CP, free cadence

Recovery 
5 minutes 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

Main Set (Repeat 2 Times) 
1 minute at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
1 minute at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
2 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
2 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
3 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm
3 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
2 minutes at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
2 minutes at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 
1 minute at 90–105% CP, 85–95 rpm 
1 minute at 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm

Recovery Between 
Sets 5 minutes 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

Cool Down 
3 minutes 40–55% CP 100–110 rpm

Total Time: 62 minutes 

Key coaching cues: 
Keep transitions between intensities smooth and controlled. Hold steady power during tempo and threshold efforts without drifting upward. Maintain relaxed upper-body posture and consistent breathing throughout. During the main set, focus on smooth cadence and stable power as durations increase. Use recoveries to reset technique and breathing before the next block.

Safety Note: 
Only undertake vigorous exercise if you are fit and healthy to do so. If you are at all unsure, consult a Physician or Doctor first. All training equipment including Bikes and Turbo trainers should be in full working order. Do not use any piece of equipment that does not come up to the required standard.
More information:

name: VO2 Max 40/20
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

Today, we'll be aiming for around 16mins of VO2 Max time and incorporating a 40/20 interval approach which will challenge you for sure! Let's make it happen today! REMINDER: You can always adjust the FTP bias via the arrow keys on your keyboard, or the Zwift Companion app. Once you get over threshold, using a %FTP for workout prescription can get murky, so always adjust as needed

WORKOUT DESIGNER

Shayne Gaffney (GC Coaching) holds a bachelors degree in Health Science in Professional Development and Advanced Patient Care, is a USA Cycling Level 1 (expert level) Certified Coach, a level 2 certified Training Peaks coach, a USA Cycling certified power based training coach, USA Olympic Committee Safe Sport Certified, and a licensed physical therapist assistant.  He is also the creator of Zwift's "Build Me Up" Flexible Training Plan.  He can be contacted directly via  for any cycling or training related questions.

For more information on GC Coaching, please visit www.gaffneycyclingcoaching.com

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop. 

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level. For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Alpe | Week 5
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from
Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and
climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.
Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift
These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to
play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder
bike choices.
• No draft regardless of bike.
• No power up’s just you and your watts.
• Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only
10km, elevation is primary focus.
• Category enforced, must wear HRM.
• Zwift Power league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to Zwift ITT
Racing. Links below, each month the leagues will be reset. An excel backup is available
on Torturefest Cult discord ITT Climbing room.
• Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice
dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
• What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has
multiple climbs?
• How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?
One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing
Russian roulette style.

Come join Zwift TT Club on Zwift for more Time Trial event information! https://www.zwift.com/clubs/b3d1a903-df49-44eb-9c6f-4ba9f0622efe/home

Join us as we embark on a series of events - each week you will have multiple chances to set your best time on the same route!

Over the course of the series, we’ll be using routes in the region of 15-25km.

Check out Zwiftpower.com after your event to see how well you stack up against the competition!

Don’t forget to check you’re using the fastest bike frame and wheels available to you!

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? 
For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H 

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

name: Zwift Crit Racing Club - Castle Crit
description:
It's Crit time! Come and join in the fun on a number of multi-lap short routes. Get ready to dig deep and push to the finish line!

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

name: Cycle Nation Nightcrawler Ride
description:
Whether it’s early morning or late at night, depending on where you are in the world, this is where the Nightcrawlers come together for a steady, social sub-1.8 w/kg endurance ride.

No racing. No attacks. Just smooth, consistent riding with a great bunch of people who enjoy clocking up kilometres together. It’s the perfect ride to build aerobic fitness, spin the legs, and enjoy the company of cyclists from around the world.

Our experienced ride leaders keep the pace steady and the group together, making it ideal for both experienced Zwifters and those new to group rides.

If you’re looking for a relaxed, welcoming ride that never goes out of style, Tuesday is where it all begins.

The Classic. The original. The Nightcrawlers.

Connect with Cycle Nation

🌐 www.cyclenation.co.za

name: NPRC - Run Every Day Powered By NoblePro
description:
Come and join the fastest growing running club on Zwift.  With a choice of 5 or 10k you can pick your distance. Whether you are a beginner or experienced runner come and join us, you can run at whatever pace you like, it’s not a race unless you want it to be!

Each day is a different route and as new routes are released the courses will change to allow you to bag that badge.

You will run in our in game NPRC jersey and if you complete the event you get to keep it to wear wherever you like.

We also hold special events where you can win an actual jersey to wear in real life.

NPRC Facebook – We have a facebook group where you can join and talk about all things running.  Share your stories and get help and advice.

https://www.facebook.com/groups/1223724692417314/

NoblePro: - We are a team focused on elevating running through our treadmills and digital platforms. We create treadmills loved by runners and the wider running community for quality engineered hardware features and advanced software integration to give you the freedom to train with the apps you love.
https://www.noble-pro.com/

Kinni:- In a fitness world where treadmill bluetooth integration can be a confusing place, we aim to provide you with the ability to effortlessly connect. name: Team Vitality Group Social Ride
description: This is a medium paced, fun ride at the bottom to middle of the C category. It is not a race, but there will be times we can have a go at the Sprints or KOM’s for bit of fun. The average speed for the ride is aprx 32kph and the average watts/kilo is 2.0 to 2.4 each week, although the nature of the courses can cause this to vary. We aim for a steady ride with moments for recovery after crunch moments.

name: Vitality for UNICEF Group Ride
description:
Vitality, in partnership with UNICEF, is teaming up with Zwift for a series of great social rides for a fantastic cause. Don’t miss out. Join our social rides of 45 minutes to one hour and do your part to give kids a head start. Keeping you active and helping Vitality and UNICEF vaccinate millions of children worldwide.

We encourage everyone to stay together for this social ride. Every ride completion will help UNICEF vaccinate a child against polio.

About Vitality:
 
Guided by a core purpose of making people healthier, Vitality is the leader in shared-value by creating healthy behavior changes in insurance. By blending technology, data, incentives, and behavioural science, Vitality inspires healthy changes in individuals and organizations. 

In partnership with UNICEF, Vitality aims to vaccinate millions of children against polio by donating vaccines on behalf of participants who complete the Vitality for UNICEF Ride series events.

Furthermore, the partnership with Zwift has been established as part of Vitality’s global pledge to get 100 million people 20% more active by 2025 through incentives to live healthier, more active lifestyles.

description:
Start your day on the right foot or the left. Come to our 5k at your own pace (AYOP). Run, walk, chat, laugh and get your day moving on a positive note! Attitude is 90% of any situation so let’s make this day the best day and get you in the best mindset so you can be the best you!

name: INC Relentless Intervals
description:
This is a Team Time Trial Training session. Expect a hard interval session. The front of this ride will suit Category A riders, however other categories are welcome and encouraged to join and complete the workout in your own gruppettos.

These are no sweep training rides; if you drop from the group, simply continue the workout on your own or with others of a similar pace.
This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest you can draft!

name: Team Italy - Smile! It's Tuesday Ride
description:
Join the Team Italy Smile! It's Tuesday Ride each week, we’ll roll as a group at a moderate 2.5-3 w/kg pace. The course varies each week, with a range of undulating routes. These rides are perfect towards Zwifters that are looking for a varied content one hour session that can give them a full 5 zone workout. Draft in the group and stay zone 1-3, or move to the front and join the sprints for zones 4 and 5 for short bursts.

Our sweeper team will help you, if requested. Experience with group rides is of advantage - we will use the power of the group to go fast, please follow the Leader (yellow) istructions, the fence is the red barrier behind the leader, if you overtake for 60 seconds it will kick out of the ride, so respect the Leader pace, if you have extra watts you can help our sweepers Team. 

Please Add the tag Ita into your surname. When you finished the ride You will earn the Team Italy Jersey, check your Zwift Garage. If you like our events join our Companion Club Team Italy,  Facebook Group https://www.facebook.com/groups/zwiftitaly  Telegram https://t.me/ZwiftTeamItaly
#TeamItaly #Respect4Leader

name: Vikings Valhalla Tuesday Climb
description:
Welcome to the ‘Vikings Valhalla Tuesday Climb’. Are you ready to do some climbing at a pace that suits you and have a great time as well? We will supply quality leads and sweeps, all you need to do is be ready to sweat! We have two groups to accommodate different rider levels, if you find yourself in "no mans land" jump in and help sweep to get that little extra burn. Our rides are very inclusive with a "no one gets dropped" approach. We encourage riders to respect the leader's pace and ride with the yellow beacon. This is NOT A RACE! As mentioned, stronger riders are encouraged to fall back and help sweep the riders struggling in/off the back. If you are looking for a fun ride with a great group of people then, this is the
perfect ride for you!

For more information about our rides go to: https://www.facebook.com/groups/503388660165279/

name: PAOLO BARBERA MINEFIELD
description:
Please visit www.heycoach.it or contact me 

Coach Paolo Barbera is a Certified Triathlon and Ironman Coach and the founder of Active Kids, a sporting clinic to help children and adults in the prevention and treatment of obesity through healthy nutrition and tailored training programmes.

Paolo is an experienced triathlete and cyclist. In 2017 he opened an innovative endurance training centre in milan, Tri60, specialized in indoor cycling.

It has been proven that Indoor cycling plays a key role to build strength, resistance and improve overall fitness and technical skills.

Paolo’s workouts are designed to mix different training zones aiming to maximize results in a very short time. Athletes following his workouts, at the right intensity and at the right cadence, have achieved surprising results.

Paolo’s indoor cycling workouts have different lengths to meet every athlete needs.

In the last ten years Paolo has developed very successful training programs for triathletes and cyclists

IT IS NOT HOW YOU START BUT HOW YOU FINISH!

GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normaL event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests to face every workout at the right difficulty level.

name: EVO CC Vortex Interval Ride [~3-3.8w/kg avg]
description:
Welcome to the Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] interval session. These rides are geared towards Zwifters that are looking for a varied content, one hour session that can give them a full 5 zone workout. Draft in the group and stay zone 1-3, or move to the front and join the sprints for zones 4 and 5 for short bursts. Average for this ride will be mid to high Category B but it may vary based upon course/leader. There will be keepers at the back, and they will try hard to save dropped riders. The group is based upon high social interaction so bring your best banter. Use the mobile app or a keyboard to communicate in-ride.

#evo

name: Tango Tuesday
description: The QueenBees are a group of women who share a love of cycling. Just as a hive works together to bring out the best in every member of the community, so do we. We strive to support, empower and encourage women to live their best lives, no matter where they are on their life, cycling or fitness journey. name: EVO CC Flux Ride [1.8 - 2.0w/kg avg]
description:
This is a Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] Social Event and ride for all. Your co-operation and teamwork is essential to the success of the ride and we ask that all riders respect the pace set by the leader (Yellow Beacon). We may include intervals over and below the ride average advertised power range, but we will allow enough recovery and time to regroup after every effort. This is not a race, so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong we would welcome any help offered by stronger riders to bring any dropped riders back to the yellow beacon. We welcome good chat and a social atmosphere for new and experienced Zwifters alike, everyone is welcome.

#evo

name: INC Relentless Intervals
description:
Suitable for A riders as a base session, or B & C riders wanting to push themselves.

Examples of the drills are – Z2 with 15sec Z5/6 bursts every 6minutes, alternating Z2/Z3 in various durations, Z2 - Z4 ramps of decreasing duration and many other sessions.  

All sessions will be around 60-90mins and will include a warm up so just grab your bottles and head straight to the pen.

This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest surf the draft. This training ride is part of the INC RELENTLESS training rides that happen daily with each day focusing on a different area of improvement. 

Tips: Use the draft to rest and ensure you do not lose the draft.

name: Team Valhalla Early/Late Everybody's In Spin
description:
Welcome everyone short, tall, large, small and in between to our Tuesday Team Valhalla Early/Late Everybody’s In Spin.

This is D category GROUP ride with the aim to ride as a group at a pace that is inclusive and empathetic to everyone from the seasoned rider to the first timer. The advertised pace is 1.6-2W/KG.

Do you have tired legs or are you early morning pre-espresso fatigued - then this is the ride for you.

Is it a late night or afternoon and you are getting ready for supper or bed - then this is the ride for you.

Are you new to Zwift or Group Rides and worry about getting dropped or worry about a Lead that doesn’t care to help those out back? - then this is the ride for you.

This is a “no-drop” “GROUP” ride around D or Recovery pace so if you do find yourself off the back then just shout out early and there will always be a friendly face to keep you company and help get you back to the Yellow Beacon. All you have to bring is your smile. If you are a stronger rider looking for an extra challenge we would encourage you to help sweep riders off the back.

The 6 goals of this group ride are simple: 1) ride near/with the yellow beacon, 2) enjoy each other’s company/make new friends, 3) be positive, 4) engage in the banter, 5) Big the Blob and 6) HAVE FUN.

We want this ride and all our Vikings and Valhalla Rides to be a great ride experience for Everyone!!

Please check out our Facebook group at: https://www.facebook.com/groups/503388660165279/?ref=share

name: SZR Early Birdies
description:
Welcome to SZR Early birdies

This is a group ride with the focus on remaining together. You should aim to sit between the yellow and red beacon. Follow ride leader instructions at all times.

We will ride at an average pace of 2.5 w/kg prior to any race finish. The race finish is at the discretion of the ride leader and will vary in length dependent on the ride.

If there are any sprints allowed during the ride please regroup on the yellow beacon immediately after.

After hills we will focus on getting the back of the group together with the front.

#SZR

name: 3R SPARK Steady State Ride [~2.0-2.2 w/kg avg]
description: This is a 3R Group Ride Event (not a race). 3R Spark runs five days a week and is designed to be an accessible and sociable training session, aimed primarily at riders in Cat-D. Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.0-2.5 W/kg. The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides. Mondays and Tuesdays are our entry-level steady-state rides, where we aim to hold a steady 2.0-2.2 throughout. Thursdays and Fridays are our interval sessions, designed to help Cat D riders push themselves a little further. For interval sessions we aim to average between 2.2-2.5 for the session, but there will be times above and below. Thursday and Friday sessions often include an optional mini-race at the end. Wednesday is the Taylor Zwift Fan Club ride, a led by the hosts of the popular podcast of the same name – expect a sociable steady-state session with lots to keep you entertained! The TZFC ride is livestreamed at twitch.tv/TaylorZwiftFC. Rides are typically around an hour long. Spark is a great introduction to group rides on Zwift, we are a friendly and supportive group who love to see one another succeed. We always have a sweeper (red beacon) whose wheel you can grab if you get dropped. There’s always plenty of good chat, via in-ride messages or on Discord. Come and join us! Join the 3R Facebook group for more info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team 3R #3R #RideRaceRaise

name: 3R VOLT Interval Ride [~2.6-3.2 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack. 3R VOLT runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.8-3.2 w/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides and training needs, the following is a typical week:
Monday – After what has hopefully been a fun backed weekend on the bike, this our recovery session
Tuesday – Tends to be more of a classic interval session, riders usually finish with an average of around 3.0w/kg
Wednesday – We take to the hills and one of our tougher sessions with riders averaging around 3.2w/kg
Thursday – is our no red beacon ride and again tough interval sets and riders finishing around 3.2w/kg
Friday - is a little different, we don't take ourselves too seriously and often play a variety of games and quizzes along side the intervals and riders end up with around 2.8-3.0w/kg

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some may take up to 75mins with the majority finishing with either a ramp or a mini race.

The group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the VOLT discord server and features a friendly bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

This group ride is not a race so. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

description:
This is a 3R Group Ride Event. 3R Octane runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 3.2-3.8 W/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides, including weekly recovery, or transitional, rides which are usually on a Monday. Short, high intensity intervals, longer sweetspot intervals, flying laps, long and short climbs and exploring little used routes all feature.

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some can be up to two hours long, and all end with a mini race.

The Group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the Octane discord server and features a super bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. name: NPRC - Run Every Day Powered By NoblePro
description:
Come and join the fastest growing running club on Zwift.  With a choice of 5 or 10k you can pick your distance. Whether you are a beginner or experienced runner come and join us, you can run at whatever pace you like, it’s not a race unless you want it to be!

Each day is a different route and as new routes are released the courses will change to allow you to bag that badge.

You will run in our in game NPRC jersey and if you complete the event you get to keep it to wear wherever you like.

We also hold special events where you can win an actual jersey to wear in real life.

NPRC Facebook – We have a facebook group where you can join and talk about all things running.  Share your stories and get help and advice.

https://www.facebook.com/groups/1223724692417314/

NoblePro: - We are a team focused on elevating running through our treadmills and digital platforms. We create treadmills loved by runners and the wider running community for quality engineered hardware features and advanced software integration to give you the freedom to train with the apps you love.
https://www.noble-pro.com/

Kinni:- In a fitness world where treadmill bluetooth integration can be a confusing place, we aim to provide you with the ability to effortlessly connect. You can run structured treadmill workouts, connect and integrate with your favourite bluetooth fitness apps such as Zwift, Rouvy, Kinomaps and many more. We are focused on progress and advancement in integration, connectivity and control.

name: Bens Bash
description:
Training ride open to all. The aim of these rides is to provide a regular training ride for all to join in, riding at a steady pace that for some will feel challenging but over time you will get fitter and more comfortable.

Be mindful of your pace and try to keep the group together rather than just ride off on your own - look at this as a way to improve your fitness as well as pick up some skills around riding with others. 

Try not to ride over 3.5 w/kg but if you are feeling frisky - feel free to open the taps with 10 mins to go. 

We will vary the routes so check back regularly.

name: Fellowship Championship - Stage 2 - Sprint
description:
Welcome Adventurers,

Speed, positioning, and split-second timing. Stage 2 takes us to the neon-lit streets of Makuri for three blisteringly fast laps around the Sprinter's Playground. While the profile is predominantly flat, short punchy rollers will tempt aggressive breakaways. Protect your position in the wheels, conserve energy, and unleash your Aero powerup for what promises to be a high-speed bunch gallop.

Do you have what it takes to win the Fellowships first ever official Zwift Cup of Doom?

Other Rules:
Neutralised bikes
HRM Required

#fellowshipchampionship

name: GXY SURGE
description:
EVENT DESCRIPTION

Part of the SURGE group of events, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday at the same time.  

This event brings a different workout structure each of the four days of the week.  This may include power pyramids, intervals and chase strategies.  Expect a fun social event where sprints and Kom segments may be included.

EVENT DYNAMICS

Category    - D

Power 	    - 1.6 > 2.5wkg but expect the event to finish around 2.1wkg based on a 75kg rider.

Fence 	    - Will be set to KICK! used at the leader's discretion

Draft	    - Enabled – focus required to stay within the group

Sweeper     - Yes! Red beacon and beacon support riders will have a GXY tag after their name

ETHOS 

We at GXY are committed to creating a culture of belonging, inclusivity and compassion empowering people to grow stronger, work together and support one another to achieve shared success on Zwift

GXY – Here together, for you 💜

Paolo is an experienced thriathlete and cyclist, in 2017 opened an endurance training center in milan, Tri60, specilized in indoor training.

name: Compass Community Cycling Thriving Tuesday
description:
Join our social group ride on Zwift — steady effort, good company, and just enough challenge to keep it interesting.

We’ll ride together through a mix of intervals: some short and sharp, others longer and steadier. It’s about turning the pedals, keeping each other going, and sharing the miles.

Each session usually runs two weeks in a row so you can ride it once, then ride it again and notice the difference. Little by little, you’ll find the effort feels smoother, the breathing steadier, the legs that bit stronger.

The chat is open, the music is loud, and there’s always room for some laughs along the way. Drop into the conversation, share how it’s going, or just sit in and spin — it’s your ride.

Recovery isn’t just for the legs. It’s a mental reset, too.





⚠️ Important note
• This is a social group ride, not a formal coaching session.
• Everyone rides at their own pace and you join at your own risk. Please ride within your personal limits and listen to your body.
• The leader and club are volunteers and accept no responsibility for injury, illness, or equipment issues arising from participation.

Show up. Spin steady. Grow stronger together. See you on the start line.

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Alpe | Week 5
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from
Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and
climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.
Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift
These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to
play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder
bike choices.
• No draft regardless of bike.
• No power up’s just you and your watts.
• Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only
10km, elevation is primary focus.
• Category enforced, must wear HRM.
• Zwift Power league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to Zwift ITT
Racing. Links below, each month the leagues will be reset. An excel backup is available
on Torturefest Cult discord ITT Climbing room.
• Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice
dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
• What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has
multiple climbs?
• How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?
One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing
Russian roulette style.

name: Heffron Handicap
description:
Heffron Handicap

Heffron is widely regarded as the hardest regular handicap in Australia. The quality of riders, the technical course, the history and the handicap format make Heffron the legendary race that it is. As the saying goes, “if you can win at Heffron, you can win anywhere”.

Like every Heffron, expect a blistering start, followed by settling into an uncomfortably hard rhythm and watching the other grades in the last few minutes, hoping yours is the one that takes the win. Solo or mini break a few km’s from the line or an all-out sprint with 400m to go? That’s the age-old question that Heffron asks every race. The answer? Well, that changes too often to know. Win and you can say you’ve won Heffron – and know that if you win at Heffron, you can win anywhere. Get it wrong and all you’ll be left with are the “I could have won, if only” stories we tell our mates the next day. In the end, there can only be one Heffron winner.

name: AusCycling Talent Identification
description:
Your journey to the top step starts in your living room.

AusCycling invites you to test yourself against the best. The workout comprises three free ride efforts: 15 seconds, 3 minutes and 12 minutes designed to test your critical power. As with any test or race, ensure you are appropriately warmed up and motivated.

The test is short and sharp, requiring maximum commitment. Erg mode will be turned off during the intervals, you are on your own and its your time to shine.

As you fade through the efforts, use your gears to reduce the resistance and maintain your cadence. Aiming for 90-100rpm for the efforts. Finish the efforts completely spent, the key is to finish all the efforts regardless of how much your power fades or how hard it feels.

Saddle up and enjoy the ride!

 Target Audience;
 16-22yo with no high-performance sport background
 People with vision or physical impairment – any age

People with background in high-performance sport – any age
*If you are outside the ages of 16-22 and have a background in high performance sport or vision/physical impairment please visit https://www.auscycling.org.au/page/virtual-tid and contact us for more information.

Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

name: Orange Unicorn Lite
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

Making workouts less monotonous and fun is a crucial aspect of indoor training. Over/unders is an excellent way to accomplish this. Today's workout is an efficient workout to help boost our threshold power. After a warm-up, we'll go into 2 sets of 6x (2min under and 30sec over), then cool down. You got this!

WORKOUT DESIGNER

Shayne Gaffney (GC Coaching) holds a bachelors degree in Health Science in Professional Development and Advanced Patient Care, is a USA Cycling Level 1 (expert level) Certified Coach, a level 2 certified Training Peaks coach, a USA Cycling certified power based training coach, USA Olympic Committee Safe Sport Certified, and a licensed physical therapist assistant.  He is also the creator of Zwift's "Build Me Up" Flexible Training Plan.  He can be contacted directly via  for any cycling or training related questions.

For more information on GC Coaching, please visit www.gaffneycyclingcoaching.com

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.

HELPFUL HINT

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level. 

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift
